violations.text: The Person in charge did not assure compliance with critical code requirements. Management's plan for assessing, monitoring, and controlling foodborne disease hazards is inadequate. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety at all times when time temperature control for safety (TCS) food is being prepared, handled, and/or served. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the 3-bay sink was 0 parts per million (ppm). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200-400 ppm. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Assorted samosas and dumplings observed held at 46-50 degrees Fahrenheit in the front display case. Disposed. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Soups, rice, chicken, korma, and cooked vegetables observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation, and/or the date the previously prepared frozen foods are thawed. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Tofu was placed hot in the refrigerator in covered plastic containers greater than four inches deep. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Tofu was placed hot in the refrigerator in covered plastic containers greater than four inches deep. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026
Food observed stored on the floor in the walk in cooler, walk in freezer, and basement storage area. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Staff were observed not wearing hair restraints. Food employees must wear hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings, or nets that are worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment/utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Single service items are not being stored properly in their original protective package and/or are stored on a surface that is not clean in the basement storage area. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026
Single-use items observed being used for food preparation and storage. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

The display case was not in good repair, not holding food at 41 degrees or below. Display case is not to be used for foods requiring refrigeration until it has been serviced. Service was called during inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

The non-food contact surfaces of the display case including door tracks, and the single burner unit have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment or items including numerous used food containers, egg cartons, cardboard, and plastic bins to be returned were observed in the basement storage and dumpster areas. Establishments shall be kept free of unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment and litter to prevent harborage conditions. New Violation. Correct By: 05/28/2026

Raw animal foods (eggs) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (sauces, vegetables) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. New Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023

Various prepared foods were observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. New Violation. Correct By: 11/22/2023
Various food products were observed stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler and freezer. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. New Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023
Single use items are being used for food preparation and storage. New Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023

Single service items are not being stored properly in their original protective package and/or are stored on a surface that is not clean in the basement and front service area. New Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023
The thermometer in the refrigerator in the front area was not in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 11/09/2023
The non-food contact surfaces of the display case have an accumulation of food residue, and other debris. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023

The condensate from the display case refrigeration unit is draining into a container in the basement. Condensate drainage and other nonsewage liquids must drain into a drain. New Violation. Correct By: 02/08/2024
The door in the walk-in freezer is in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 12/06/2023

Unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment or items, especially recycleable containers were observed in the area near the kitchen door, and in the basement. Establishments shall be kept free of unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment and litter to prevent harborage conditions. New Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023

The floors especially beneath the rolling bins stored below the food prep counter have an accumulation of soil residue and/or food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 11/08/2023
